lines.text: Four days later, the Skeld came out of the White. Two hundred people and forty sledges, walking onto the warm grass of the north field as if it were a dream.
The frost on that field was gone by evening. Yrsa said the land was happy to see me. I said it was probably the drainage.
And on the first sledge, under hides, was the first load from the Deep.
My lord. I've worked rimeglass for a year. I've never seen glass like this. Not even in my grandfather's notes.
One sledge. I make it forty thousand crowns. Ten times the debt that nearly sank us.
Bram sat down. Bram never sits down.
We were rich. For about an hour.
Then a cart came up the south road. One tired horse, and one man.
My lord. Don't get up. I've come to tell you something you're going to hate.
Lady Sabine bought every debt I owed. My ships. My warehouses. My good name. All hers.
And every guild in the midlands has sworn off rimeglass. Buy Greyhollow glass, and you'll never sell anything south of the Senn again.
Forty thousand crowns of glass. And nobody left who dared to buy it.
I did manage to keep one thing, my lord. The coat. A man has to have standards.
And the Order still thinks you've spent three weeks in bed with a cold.
Three weeks gone. Three left, perhaps less, before a royal warrant came up that same south road. With soldiers behind it.
Then Bram gave me three letters. They had come while I was away. Three seals. Three northern lords.
To the boy at Greyhollow. They tell me you make the north warm. I'd like to see that with my own eyes. Kesting.
Lady Ysolde Marrick would be delighted to discuss the price of warmth.
Lord Penhallow sends his compliments. And his curiosity.
They all want to meet the boy who makes the north warm.
Sabine had closed the south to us. Fine. Then we would stop looking south.
Bram. If the lords of the north want to see me, they can all see me at once.
We'll hold a Moot.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter forty-three, coming soon.
